title: Trim CLAUDE.md and delete retired Claude Code artifacts
description: AGENTS.md, .codex/ repo-local config, and the ECK-derived .claude/skills/handover skill are retired: opum-handoff in the opum-workflow plugin replaces the handover skill, and Codex is retired as this fleet internal runtime. lore init --codex stays (public product surface); only repo-local Codex config goes. Also strip .claude/settings.local.json of the backlog permission entry and the two absolute-path hooks into opum-agent tooling/opum-fleet/hooks (plugin hooks.json covers Notification/Stop at user scope now). CLAUDE.md drops from 512 lines to about 200 by removing the 38 references to Treehouse, Backlog, Codex, herdr, AGENTS.md, and opum-worktrees that this repo profile still carries, without touching the byte-identical fleet operating block between the opum:fleet-operating markers.

acceptanceCriteria.text: AGENTS.md and .codex/ are removed from the repo once LCLI-442 lands, with lore agent-bridge product code for init --codex left intact
git grep finds no reference to Treehouse, the deleted Backlog CLI, herdr hook paths, or opum-worktrees in CLAUDE.md repo-owned prose
settings.local.json no longer allows the backlog CLI or points at opum-agent tooling hook paths
lore check exits 0 and quest agents --check --require-installed exits 0 after the changes

implementationNotes: HOLD on deleting AGENTS.md/.codex/ this pass. Baseline before any edits: quest agents --check --require-installed exits 6, drift, because the ONLY Quest-managed instructions block in this repo lives inside AGENTS.md's <!-- quest:agent-instructions:begin --> section (pinned to Quest CLI 0.3.1 vs installed 0.3.2) -- CLAUDE.md carries a separately-authored, hand-critical Quest Workflow block, not the machine-managed one. Deleting AGENTS.md now would make this task's own AC (quest agents --check --require-installed exits 0) mechanically unsatisfiable, and repeats the gap opum-agent's own OPAG-35 note already recorded after doing exactly this: quest writes its managed block only to AGENTS.md, so the check now reports it missing with no supported alternative home. opum-agent OPAG-41 (To Do) is the task tracking that upstream fix, and its own AC reads: AGENTS.md is deleted from all five repos only after the upstream change lands. AGENTS.md itself also carries a header comment warning that deleting it as a Codex artifact already broke opum-agent assertNoMigrationLaunchFence fleet-wide once, on 2026-08-30. Filed LCLI-442 as this repo half of the OPAG-41 upstream fix, and added it as a dependency here. Proceeding this pass with: quest agents --update-instructions (fixes the pre-existing 0.3.1 to 0.3.2 drift, unrelated to this decision), the handover skill deletion, settings.local.json cleanup, and a CLAUDE.md trim of everything except the AGENTS.md-coupled content. Reported to opum-agent-41 for a ruling; will delete AGENTS.md/.codex/ on their word or once LCLI-442 lands.

Section list for your review, applying the every-session-start vs reference-material test, honestly rather than defensively:

Grep used to confirm no retired machinery outside the fleet block (lines 35-206): awk 'NR==35{f=1} NR==206{f=0} f==0' CLAUDE.md | grep -inE "treehouse|opencode|\bcodex\b.*(runtime|worker)|opum-worktrees|backlog (task|instructions|handover)|FMC\b" -- 3 hits, all legitimate: (1) confirms absence of Treehouse/Codex detection code, (2) confirms lore init --codex is kept product surface not retired machinery, (3) confirms backlog/ and OpenCode Worker are correctly described as already-retired history. None instruct using anything retired.

Sections, current order:
- Quest Workflow (managed block) -- PASSES: explicit every-request instruction.
- lore-cli repo profile / Role, Retirement machinery, What other repos read, Constraints and couplings -- PASSES: dev-vs-main gate asymmetry, the ci.yml/dev coupling, and the AGENTS.md hold are exactly the facts that silently corrupt any branch/PR/deletion decision regardless of task.
- Product portfolio and cross-repository routing (routing pointers, DNS ownership, five traps) -- PASSES, arguably: each trap is a silent-corruption risk on an unrelated task (wrong GitHub org, stale visibility assumption, wrong peer-reaching method), kept short with pointers to the fuller docs/reference pages.
- Writing a rule down here -- BORDERLINE, leaning FAILS: this is authoring guidance for whoever next edits this file's prose, not something a session doing ordinary task work touches. Candidate to move to a docs/reference page and link it, pulled in only when someone is about to edit this section.
- The three sessions that ship this pair (pairing table + hard-constraint fact) -- PASSES: relevant to any src/adapters/quest.ts change or release coordination, which is a meaningful fraction of this repo's work.
- What actually worked, and is worth repeating (6-bullet retrospective) -- BORDERLINE, leaning FAILS: lessons-learned reference material, not a live constraint a session needs before acting. Candidate to move to docs/reference alongside lore-cli-release-truth.md.
- Project-level skills: what is here on purpose -- BORDERLINE, leaning FAILS: only relevant when someone considers adding/removing a project-level skill, a rare event, not every session.

I have not moved the three borderline sections yet -- that would mean force-pushing an already-green, open PR (#565) for a scope change you have not ruled on. Say which of the three you want moved and I will do it as a follow-up on this same branch before it lands, or as a separate LCLI task after, whichever you prefer.
